# Tiger repair quality corpus v1

This corpus was frozen by the parser/quality agent independently of the semantic implementation. `manifest.json` binds every source, literal quotation, character range and required financial interpretation. Runtime code must never consume heldout labels. A label dispute needs an independent adjudication entry, a new corpus version and rerunning affected acceptance; do not edit v1 labels to fit a model output.

Three development cases and three heldout synthetic cases are deliberately marked `TEST_FIXTURE`. Their issuers and events are invented, and they prove mechanisms only. The fourth heldout case is the full original 58,823-byte Federal Reserve G.17 response already present in the approved 237-document archive. Only its summary table, date and notes were independently labelled. The archive records its authority as `unverified`; this remains explicit and this corpus does not upgrade the original authority or publication-time metadata. Original whitespace is retained under a file-specific Git attribute; source bytes must not be reformatted. Its capture URL is mutable; the SHA256, archived document ID and original bytes bind this historical sample.

There are 23 critical labels covering financial periods, currency/unit, table columns, footnotes, entity ambiguity, republication, correction/withdrawal, counterevidence, missing required sources and future events. Factual claims and quotations must agree. Critical subject/amount/period/unit/counterevidence errors block acceptance; incomplete/unknown outputs stay in each denominator. The corpus is a small regression baseline, not evidence of a population reliability percentage, real trading returns or complete coverage of 237 originals.

The integrity test only checks frozen source/label binding and split identity. Full semantic assessment must actually run the declared entry on a frozen implementation, then independently compare its outputs with these labels. Record first-pass versus repaired pass, original sample counts, failures, unknown outcomes, profile, contract and timing. Keep market outcomes separate from process, source, semantic and risk failures; later material cannot become prior evidence.

Parser API: use trusted `ParsePolicy(manifest_version="v1")` for new work; omitted/None preserves historical normalization and policy serialization. `result.metadata["parse_manifest"]` carries original/text hashes, extraction units, locator coordinate systems, omitted units, attachment discovery and publication/revision/retrieval/unknown event times. HTML locators address decoded original HTML; Scrapling locators address deterministically reconstructed selected markup (hash and pinned engine policy included). PDF locators address extracted page text, never visual bounding boxes. PDF table/footnote layout remains unverified and blank/scanned pages require review. Original bytes remain available unchanged.

`ParserResourcePool` provides atomic memory/temp/worker reservations for one coordinator process. Pass the same pool to concurrent `extract_response(..., resource_pool=pool)` calls. Rejection occurs before worker spawn; no request is retried. Multi-process scheduling must reserve at the persistent scheduler. Pool limits are trusted operator settings, not document-controlled. Runtime measurements remain outside deterministic source evidence. The existing default parser limits remain 60 seconds, 32 MiB input, 16 MiB text, 768 MiB child memory, 1000 pages; v1 adds an explicit 100,000 structural-element ceiling, disk-space preflight and ENOSPC/EDQUOT classification.

Official parser limitation reference: [pypdf text extraction](https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/extract-text.html), read during this implementation. Text extraction does not supply OCR or guarantee table/footnote structure; the new manifest therefore records those gaps instead of treating any nonempty PDF as complete.
